alerts.reason: Farmer Brothers’ year-over-year sales growth slowed from 19.57% in June to 12.01% in September. Unit volume fell 11.4%, concentrated among direct-ship customers, while average unit price rose 26.4% (B, D). I forecast that pricing keeps December above −5%. If the volume decline persists, a price gain of about 7.2% or less in January–March would take net sales to −5% or worse.

Brooks’ quarterly revenue growth slowed from 2.83% in June to 0.46% in September, despite 8% growth for the full fiscal year (A). Lockdowns had periodically reduced customer demand for services and travel restrictions had limited service delivery (C). I forecast a modest December decline above −5%, followed by a decline of at least 5% in January–March if service disruptions persist.

Kadant’s bookings fell from $265.9 million to $210.9 million in one quarter, down 13.8% year over year, while reported revenue still grew 12.4% (A, B). Earlier orders should support December shipments. The smaller pool of new orders leads me to forecast a reported revenue decline of at least 5% in January–March.

Tennant’s reported sales moved from 0.39% growth in June to a 3.35% decline in September. Higher prices across all regions were still supporting sales as component shortages reduced volume (C, D). I forecast that pricing holds December above −5% and that continued shipment constraints push January–March below that threshold. From September, the gap was only 1.65 percentage points.

ACI’s year-over-year revenue change swung from +12.85% in June to −3.26% in September, when revenue fell $10.3 million (A). Its licensing and capacity-upgrade sales depend partly on customers needing more transaction capacity (C). I forecast December stays above −5% and January–March reaches −5% or worse. The timing is uncertain because the filing gives no schedule for those sales.

Insight’s year-over-year sales gain narrowed from $513.9 million in June to $86.8 million in September, cutting growth from 23.05% to 3.55%. Sales fell $209.0 million between those quarters while the prior-year comparison rose $218.0 million. I forecast growth stays above −5% in December and crosses to −5% or worse in January–March, with lower confidence in the timing because the signal comes from sales history.

AXT’s revenue fell 10.9% sequentially as year-over-year growth slowed from 17.05% to 1.76%. Customers also filed more warranty claims over quality issues (C), creating a risk to repeat orders. I forecast a December result above −5%, followed by a January–March decline of at least 5% as weaker orders affect shipments.

Covenant’s year-over-year revenue growth slowed from 23.82% to 13.58%. Expedited and Dedicated still grew and supplied 68% of revenue (A, C, D), supporting a December result above −5%. Two more quarters of deceleration at the recent 10.24-percentage-point pace would put year-over-year growth near +3% in December and −7% in January–March.

Schneider’s reported revenue growth slowed from 28.37% to 15.98%. Dedicated volume and acquired revenue still supported sales, while network volumes and productivity fell (A, B). A repeat of the 12.4-point slowdown would leave December near +3.6% and put January–March near −8.8%.

Saia’s reported revenue growth slowed from 30.49% to 18.39%, and less-than-truckload shipments per workday were already down 2.5% year over year (A, B). Pricing and fuel surcharges still supported performance (D). If growth slows by another 12.1 points per quarter as shipment weakness persists, December would be near +6.3% and January–March near −5.8%.
